conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be helping take care of you tonight. You’re here because of some elbow pain and low blood counts. Can you tell me about the pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes… left elbow. Started suddenly. No injury. Goes down to hand.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any fever, swelling, or redness in the elbow?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No. Just pain when I move it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. We also noticed your blood count is very low—your hemoglobin is 5.4. That’s why you might feel more tired than usual.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But I feel okay… son says I’ve been better lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good to hear. But your stool tested positive for blood, and you’re on warfarin, which thins the blood. Your INR is 6.0—much higher than it should be.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Warfarin for clots. I know.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Because of the high INR and low blood count, we’re giving you vitamin K to reverse the warfarin and will likely give you blood transfusions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Transfusion? Is it bad?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s serious, but treatable. The bleeding is likely from your stomach or intestines. You’ve had this before, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes… black stools. But I take iron. Always dark.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Right. But the black color can also mean bleeding. We’ll monitor you closely. We’ve started the vitamin K, and you’ll get blood slowly over the next few hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your hemoglobin improved to 28.5 after two units of blood. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. Elbow feels less painful.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. The elbow pain is improving on its own. X-rays were normal, so no fracture or joint issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. But I had trouble breathing last night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your oxygen dipped to 90%. We think it’s because you got some fluid from the transfusion and your heart is a bit overloaded. We gave you Lasix to help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Heart? I have CHF.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and it’s well-managed. But with the extra fluid, it got a little stressed. We’ll keep an eye on your breathing and weight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We got your H. pylori test back—it’s positive. But your doctor said you were treated for it last year, so we won’t repeat treatment now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember that. Antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We’ll continue your pantoprazole to protect your stomach. The GI team will see you soon to talk about long-term prevention.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’ve had two more units of blood. Your hemoglobin is stable. No more bleeding from the stool.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. Can I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. We need to make sure your INR comes down and you’re not at risk for more bleeding. We reversed it with vitamin K and FFP.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And warfarin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We held it for now. Your doctor prefers to restart it, but we need to discuss the risks—bleeding again vs. risk of clots if you stop it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t want clots. Had PEs before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. So we’ll restart your usual dose, but your son should call the clinic if you eat less than usual—poor intake can raise your INR again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: He will. I eat less when I’m not feeling well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s important. We’ll check your INR soon and again after discharge. Also, weigh yourself every morning. If you gain more than 3 pounds, call your doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your INR is now 2.4—much better. We’re going to restart your warfarin tonight at your usual dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. And my heart medicine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We held your metoprolol for a bit, but we’ll restart it. Your blood pressure is stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We’re planning to discharge you today. Your hemoglobin is stable, no more bleeding, and your INR is in a safer range.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. What do I need to do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take your medications as listed: warfarin, pantoprazole, furosemide, and acetaminophen for pain. No NSAIDs, even topical, on your chest—switch to acetaminophen gel if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. CBC and INR check on the scheduled date. Call if you feel weak, dizzy, or have black stools. And weigh yourself daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for taking care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’re glad you’re feeling better. Your son will help you at home, and home health will check in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes. He’s very helpful.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll get your discharge papers ready. You should feel more energy now that your blood count is up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I already do. Much better than yesterday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s exactly what we wanted to hear. Take care, and don’t hesitate to call if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll see you in follow-up soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes. I’ll be careful.
